case_metadata.participant_note: All participant-visible evidence for this case is frozen in the evidence directory. Hidden keys are stored outside the repository.

evidence.content:
Corruption occurs only for uploads larger than 8 MiB using content-encoding zstd.
Small uploads and large uncompressed uploads are unaffected.
Affected requests all traversed proxy firmware 7.4.

Client library 5.0 introduced zstd-by-default for payloads >8 MiB.
Proxy firmware 7.4 was rolled to half the gateway fleet.
Older client 4.8 does not send zstd. Proxy 7.3 and 7.4 both pass ordinary chunked uploads.

On the failing 5.0 + 7.4 path, the proxy emits a malformed final chunk after zstd streaming crosses the 8 MiB internal buffer boundary.
The same client stream captured before proxy ingress has a valid checksum.

Routing client-5.0 traffic through proxy-7.3 eliminates corruption.
Keeping proxy-7.4 but disabling zstd on client-5.0 also eliminates corruption.
Neither mitigation changes document content before gateway processing.

candidate_causes.claim: Proxy Firmware 7.4 contains a regression in buffer management that corrupts zstd-encoded streams when they exceed the 8 MiB internal buffer boundary.
Client Library 5.0 introduced zstd-by-default for payloads >8 MiB, which triggered the existing buffer handling flaw in the proxy.

action.reason: Rolling back the proxy firmware to version 7.3 is the most direct and robust reversible mitigation. It restores the gateway to a known-good state where zstd-encoded streams (introduced by Client 5.0) can be processed without corruption, addressing the source of the defect without requiring client-side configuration changes.

evidence.claim: Proxy Firmware 7.4 is the site of corruption because corruption only occurs on this version (E01, E03) and the proxy is explicitly shown to emit malformed chunks at the 8 MiB buffer boundary (E04).

Client Library 5.0 is the trigger for the issue by introducing zstd-by-default for large payloads (E02), but the issue can be mitigated by either rolling back the proxy or disabling zstd on the client (E05).

uncertainty: The evidence does not specify if other compression types (e.g., gzip) also trigger the 8 MiB buffer corruption in Proxy 7.4, though the current issue is isolated to zstd.

next_test.test: Verify if Proxy Firmware 7.4 fails with zstd-encoded streams on payloads smaller than 8 MiB (to confirm the buffer boundary is the specific trigger) and test other compression types over 8 MiB (to determine if the bug is zstd-specific or a general buffer handling error).
next_test.outcome_a_implication: If it passes under 8 MiB, it confirms the 8 MiB buffer boundary is the specific trigger point.
next_test.outcome_b_implication: If it fails with other compression types, it indicates a general buffer management regression in the proxy firmware.
